import threading

class LRUCache:
    """
    A Least Recently Used (LRU) cache with TTL (Time To Live) expiry support.
    
    This class maintains a fixed-capacity cache where:
    - The least recently used item is evicted when the cache is full
    - Items automatically expire after their TTL has elapsed
    - Accessing an item (get) refreshes its position in the LRU order
    - Setting an item (set) either adds it or updates it and refreshes its position
    
    Time complexity:
    - get: O(1) average
    - set: O(1) average
    - __len__: O(1)
    - __contains__: O(1) average
    
    Space complexity:
    - O(n) where n is the cache capacity
    """
    
    def __init__(self, capacity: int = 100, default_ttl: Optional[float] = None):
        """
        Initialize the LRU cache.
        
        Args:
            capacity: Maximum number of items the cache can hold.
                      Must be a positive integer.
            default_ttl: Default time-to-live in seconds for items.
                         If None, items never expire by default.
                         Can be overridden per-item in set().
        
        Raises:
            ValueError: If capacity is not a positive integer.
        """
        if not isinstance(capacity, int) or capacity <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Capacity must be a positive integer, got {capacity}")
        
        self.capacity = capacity
        self.default_ttl = default_ttl

        ttl: Time to live in seconds. None means no expiry.
        accessed_count: Number of times this entry has been accessed.

    key: Hashable

    timestamp: float
    ttl: Optional[float] = None
    accessed_count: int = 1
    
    def is_expired(self, current_time: Optional[float] = None) -> bool:
        """
        Check if this cache entry has expired.
        
        Args:
            current_time: The current time. If None, uses time.time().
            
        Returns:
            True if the entry has expired, False otherwise.
        """
        if self.ttl is None:
            return False
        if current_time is None:
            current_time = time.time()
        return (current_time - self.timestamp) > self.ttl
    
    def refresh(self, new_timestamp: Optional[float] = None) -> None:
        """
        Refresh the timestamp of this entry (called on access).
        
        Args:
            new_timestamp: The new timestamp. If None, uses time.time().
        """
        if new_timestamp is None:
            new_timestamp = time.time()
        self.timestamp = new_timestamp
        self.accessed_count += 1
